headline: NASA Crew-13 Set for Record-Breaking Sprint to Space Station
meta_description: Four astronauts launch October 1 for the fastest U.S. trip to the ISS ever—just 7 hours and 50 minutes from Earth to orbit.
summary_short: NASA's SpaceX Crew-13 launches Thursday for a historic milestone: the fastest journey to the International Space Station in U.S. history.
body:
On October 1, four space explorers will blast off on a journey that rewrites the record books. NASA astronauts Jessica Watkins and Luke Delaney, Canadian Space Agency astronaut Joshua Kutryk, and Russian cosmonaut Sergey Teteryatnikov are scheduled to launch at 11:10 a.m. EDT from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida aboard a SpaceX Dragon spacecraft. If all goes according to plan, they will dock at the International Space Station just 7 hours and 50 minutes later—making it the fastest trip to the orbiting laboratory by any U.S. spacecraft in the station's 26-year history. The speed represents a dramatic leap in spaceflight efficiency, a testament to improvements in launch technology and orbital rendezvous procedures.

NASA will broadcast the entire mission live, beginning with launch coverage at 9:20 a.m. The Dragon is targeted to dock at the forward-facing port of the station's Harmony module around 7 p.m., with hatch opening and welcome remarks scheduled for 8:45 p.m. Viewers can stream the event across NASA's official platforms. The crew will then conduct a brief handover with the departing Crew-12 astronauts before settling into their extended stay conducting science and mission operations aboard the station.

What makes this achievement particularly meaningful is how it reflects the maturing partnership between NASA and commercial spaceflight. The faster journey reduces physical strain on astronauts and allows more efficient use of resources. As space exploration becomes increasingly routine yet ever more capable, milestones like these mark quiet but significant steps toward a future where regular human spaceflight to low Earth orbit is seamless and reliable.
quick_facts: Launch: October 1, 11:10 a.m. EDT from Cape Canaveral, Florida
Docking time: 7 hours 50 minutes—fastest U.S. journey to ISS ever
Crew of four: two NASA astronauts, one Canadian, one Russian cosmonaut
Live coverage begins 9:20 a.m., docking targeted for 7 p.m. EDT
